newsitem.title: USA: Dreyer Grand fined $66,500 by EPA.
newsitem.headline: Dreyer Grand fined $66,500 by EPA.

text.p: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency said it has has fined Dreyer's Grand Ice Cream Inc $66,500 after it accidently released ammonia into the air and then failed to report it to authorities immediately.

The fine is related to the March 21, 1993, accidental release of about 4,000 pounds of anhydrous ammonia, a refrigerant used by the food industry, from its City of Commerce, Calif., plant, the EPA said.
The reportable amount of ammonia is 100 pounds and requires immediate notification to the California Office of Emergency Services and the National Response Center.

During the course of the investigation, Dreyer's disclosed that the company had failed to submit timely, complete, and accurate reporting forms for ammonia emissions at facilities in City of Commerce and Union City, Calif., the EPA said.
Dreyer's was not immediately available for comment.
